To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cognitive decline is more rapid in elderly people who are male, older, have worse cognition, carry the ε4 allele, and have cognitive impairment diagnosed before an operation.
cognitive decline is accelerated by major surgery in older patients who are diagnosed with cognitive impairment at recruitment, but not in other older patients.
cognitive decline appears to accelerate in people with cognitive impairment after surgery, but not in people without cognitive impairment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects on cognition in older people of anaesthesia and surgery.
the effects of surgery and anaesthesia in the elderly.
the effects on cognition and behaviour of anaesthesia and surgery in elderly patients, and the effects on cognitive decline of genetic and other factors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cognitive decline appears to accelerate in elderly patients diagnosed cognitively impaired after major surgery.
cognitive impairment is not accelerated in elderly patients after surgery.
surgery in the elderly is not a risk factor for cognitive decline, but surgery in the elderly with cognitive impairment is.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

cognitive decline is accelerated by surgery in elderly people with pre‐existing cognitive impairment, but that surgery does not accelerate cognitive decline in elderly people without cognitive impairment.
the effects of surgery on cognition are not large, but they may be important in elderly people with cognitive impairment.
surgery and anaesthesia do not appear to accelerate cognitive decline in the general population, but that this is not true for those with cognitive impairment at the time of surgery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cognitive decline in the elderly can be accelerated by surgery, but not in all patients.
cognitive decline is more rapid in elderly patients who have surgery, but only in those who have a pre‐existing cognitive impairment.
cognitive impairment in elderly patients may accelerate after major surgery and that this is more likely to occur in patients with APOEε4.
